name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=keyboard input, descriptor=check_buffer_nonempty). Accurately describes behavior: returns true when the BIOS keyboard buffer head (0x41A) != tail (0x41C), i.e. input is pending. No Ghidra address-residue suffix; no embedded domain ID to preserve.
purpose: Poll predicate that returns true when the BIOS keyboard buffer holds pending input (head pointer != tail pointer).
logic_summary: Reads the two BIOS Data Area keyboard ring-buffer pointers via the flat DOS/4G memory model -- head at 0:0x41A and tail at 0:0x41C (asm reads each sign-extended: MOVSX EAX,word ptr [0x41a] / [0x41c]) -- and returns (tail != head). Equal pointers mean an empty buffer (returns 0/false); any difference means at least one keystroke is queued (returns 1/true). The leading PUSH 8 / CALL __CHK is the Watcom stack-probe prologue, not game logic (the in_stack_* args in the decompile are the probe's garbage stack reads, not real parameters).

returns.semantics: Nonzero (1) if the BIOS keyboard buffer has pending input (head != tail); 0 if empty. Used as the spin/poll predicate by all the input-wait loops.
